Verified against RealIsometryCompletion.lean exists_orthogonal_completion (L20-59). The theorem takes V : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin r) R, an embedding e : Fin r -> Fin N (arbitrary injective placement, not a prefix), hypothesis V^T V = 1, and produces U with U^T U = 1 and U i (e a) = V i a. The proof uses orthonormal_iff_ite, builds the column family, and invokes ho.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq (basis extension in EuclideanSpace) - exactly the three ingredients the rubric demands (V^T V = I <=> orthonormal columns with r<=N; injective placement preserves orthonormality; orthonormal-basis extension fills remaining positions). The four-part NL proof is faithful and precise. No v3 item targets RealIsometryCompletion; new core. Bare-name target_nodes defect.

Verified against TensorTrainCanonical.lean: paddedCore (L255-258, zero-pads outputs beyond the active rank), paddedCore_inactive_output (L260-262, padded output rows with r<=b.val are identically 0), complexCore_isometry (L215-226) and paddedCore_active_isometry (L295-315, the active clean-input column Gram matrix stays the identity after embedding). The counterexample (active block [1] padded to column (1,0) in dimension 2: column relation gives 1, row relation gives diag(1,0)!=I) is mathematically correct and precisely distinguishes surviving column-orthonormality from destroyed row-orthonormality - the general 'a zero row cannot satisfy row-orthonormality' reasoning is sound.
